title: Build together: the email short list
goal: Take the third piece through the six steps. You leave with an inbox review you run when you ask: everything sorted, the short list only you can act on, and reply drafts to check. It never sends.
you_need: The class starter for week 3, unzipped
The Claude app or Claude Code
Optional: ten of your own emails, with no passwords in them

steps.do: Design: Double-click Launch, press Start the six steps, and read the design note for the email short list.
steps.see: The question it answers: which emails need me, and what do I say?
steps.tip: An inbox is a to-do list that other people write. The short list is the part only you can do.

steps.do: Prompt: Find the five parts in the build prompt, then press Copy the build prompt, paste it into the Claude app or Claude Code, and send. Save the file as week-3-email.js in the pieces folder, and say yes to replace.
steps.see: Role, context, the design note, the rules, what to hand back. Then your computer asks whether to replace week-3-email.js.
steps.tip: Brief it like a new hire. A prompt is a template you fill in, not a wish.

steps.do: Review: Press I saved the file. Look again. Read the page against the design note and find the one thing it got wrong.
steps.see: 12 emails reviewed, 4 on the short list, 3 drafts to check, 1 that looks fake.
steps.tip: Look for a Send button. There must not be one.

steps.do: Test: Open Run the review, press Copy the prompt and the emails, paste into Claude and send. Bring the whole answer back and press Use this review.
steps.see: The page fills in again, this time from the AI's own answer.
steps.tip: No AI handy? Press the button that loads the sample answer.

steps.do: Test: Run the three checks. Count the four piles, move 3 invoices are overdue from FYI to Reply today, and copy one draft.
steps.see: The piles add up to 12, the short list grows by one, and nothing is sent.
steps.tip: The AI could not know what a late invoice means to you. Now the page does.

steps.do: Ship: Press How it was built, and in step 5 type your runbook line: the step, the sign it worked, how to undo it.
steps.see: Three short answers, saved as you type.
steps.tip: If your Claude plan has the Gmail connector, the review can read the inbox itself, and it only reads. If not, paste the emails in. Any mail program works.

steps.do: Log: In step 6, type what changed and why, then press Add to my change log.
steps.see: Your change log has one more line.
steps.tip: Next Wednesday: the pipeline, where every deal gets a next step and a date.

real_life: Tomorrow morning: press My business, open Email, and run the review on ten of your own emails. Leave out anything with a password or a card number.
Read every draft before you copy it. Tick I checked every fact in it only when you did.
When the review sorts an email wrong, move it, and add one line to the prompt so it gets it right next time.
if_it_breaks: The AI is slow, or the page does not show after you saved the file: take the finished week-3-email.js from the pieces folder of the complete project, save it in your pieces folder, and keep going.
The page says it could not find the review: the answer has to start with the word REVIEW and keep the shape the prompt shows. Ask the AI to hand it back again in that shape.
Start over with the sample data puts the sample review back.
